items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Sid Weiss was a good bass player, and Al Avola worked real well with me -- he was the guitar player.

ctx.x: : I'm in the same vintage as you, and you are considered during the big band era, the epitome of jazz, of a big band jazz drummer. The things that you set were the standards which Buddy Rich followed, which Dave Tough followed, which Cozy Cole followed, which all of the great big band jazz drummers followed. Now you were going to tell me -- you said that when you were with Charlie Barnet, you were trying to establish your own style, so continue with that.

Let's stay with Shaw. I was grateful to Shaw for the opportunities he gave me, as a kid learning. The rhythm section was a struggle for me -- I never came out in any of the records we made, they were all hits, they did such great things, but it was a struggle for me. Sid Weiss was a good bass player, and Al Avola worked real well with me -- he was the guitar player. The band was really swinging, and I was trying to get them to swing like Basie, and it didn't work out. I had a little problem with the piano player…
